guides.title: Getting started guides
guides.description: Four short guides to get you comfortable with NaHo in your very first session.

items.title: Start the Kaiwa learning path
items.description: Practise speaking with the Marugoto coursebook, moving from topics to individual dialogues.
steps: Open “Kaiwa learning path” in the left sidebar and pick the book that matches your level.
Choose a topic, then open the first unlocked dialogue in the path.
Grant microphone permission when your browser asks, then press record and speak along with the prompt.
When the lesson ends, read the pronunciation report and redo the sentences marked for improvement.

items.title: Run a free AI dialogue session
items.description: Choose your own scenario and AI companion to practise speaking beyond the coursebook.
steps: Open “Free AI dialogue” in the left sidebar.
Pick an AI companion whose role and level match your goal for the session.
Set the topic, difficulty and advanced options, then start the session.
Speak naturally as in a real conversation, then end the session to receive overall feedback.

items.title: Read your speaking report
items.description: Learn how to use the report after each session so you improve faster.
steps: Open the account menu in the top right corner and choose “Speaking history”.
Select a completed session to open its detailed report.
Compare what you said with the model sentence to spot mispronounced or missing sounds.
Redo the lowest-scoring sentences before moving on to a new lesson.

items.title: Build a daily habit
items.description: Check in, complete missions and hold your place on the competition leaderboard.
steps: Press “Check in” in the top bar every day to earn streak rewards.
Open “Missions” to see today's tasks and the reward attached to each one.
Complete a mission to earn L-Point, then claim the reward directly in the mission list.
Track your position on the competition leaderboard to stay motivated.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.description: The questions NaHo learners send us most often.
faq.emptyCategory: There are no questions in this topic yet.

items.question: What is NaHo and who is it for?
answer: NaHo is a Japanese speaking platform with an AI companion, built around the Marugoto coursebook. You follow a dialogue-based path, speak directly with the AI and get pronunciation feedback after every sentence.
It suits beginners who need a clear path, as well as learners who already have a foundation but lack a place to practise speaking regularly.

items.question: I am new to Japanese — where should I start?
answer: Start in the Kaiwa learning path and pick the lowest-level book. The path unlocks in order, so you never have to decide what to study next.
Once you are comfortable speaking into the microphone, add free AI dialogue sessions to practise reacting to content outside the coursebook.

items.question: What is the Marugoto coursebook used in NaHo?
answer: Marugoto is a communication-oriented Japanese coursebook organised by level and by everyday topic. NaHo uses its topic-and-dialogue structure as the backbone of the speaking path.
Every lesson maps to a concrete communication situation, so you learn patterns you can use immediately instead of isolated grammar points.

items.question: Can I change the interface language?
answer: Yes. Press the globe icon in the top bar to switch between Vietnamese, English and Japanese.
The language setting only affects the interface and help content; the Japanese lesson material stays unchanged.

items.question: How does NaHo score my pronunciation?
answer: After each sentence the system converts your speech to text and compares it with the model sentence to evaluate pronunciation accuracy, completeness and fluency.
The score is a reference to show you what to practise again. Read the detailed feedback rather than focusing on the overall number.

items.question: How is the Kaiwa path different from free AI dialogue?
answer: The Kaiwa path follows the Marugoto coursebook: fixed content, sequential unlocking and a report for every lesson. It keeps you on a structured route.
Free AI dialogue is not tied to a lesson: you pick the scenario, companion and difficulty yourself. It is where you apply what you have learned.

items.question: Can I choose the AI companion and the difficulty?
answer: Yes. On the free AI dialogue setup screen, each companion has its own role and level to suit different situations.
In the advanced options you can adjust the topic and difficulty of the session before you start.

items.question: Where can I review my completed speaking sessions?
answer: Open the account menu in the top right corner and choose “Speaking history”. The list shows completed sessions with their time and results.
Select any session to open its detailed report.

items.question: What is L-Point?
answer: L-Point is what you earn by completing lessons, daily missions and check-ins. It determines your position on the competition leaderboard.
You can review every point transaction in “Point history” in the account menu.

items.question: When do daily missions reset?
answer: Missions reset every day. Missions you did not finish yesterday do not carry over to the new day.
Once you meet the requirement you still need to claim the reward in the mission list before the L-Point is added to your account.

items.question: How do daily check-in and reward chests work?
answer: You can check in once per day using the “Check in” button in the top bar. The monthly calendar lets you follow your streak.
Certain milestones in the month unlock chests with larger rewards. If you miss a day the streak restarts, but rewards you already claimed are kept.

items.question: How is the competition leaderboard calculated?
answer: Learners are placed into tiered leagues, and your rank inside a league is based on the total L-Point you accumulate during the competition period.
Studying a little every day usually beats cramming, because missions and check-ins only award points on a per-day basis.

items.question: I finished a session but my points did not increase
answer: First check whether the lesson was recorded as completed — a session you exited halfway is not counted.

For daily missions, points only arrive after you claim the reward. If everything looks correct but the points are still missing, reload the page and check “Point history”; if they are still absent, send a report to support.

items.question: Can I use NaHo for free?
answer: You can create an account and explore the open content at no cost. Some advanced content and usage limits require a paid plan.
The full list of plans and what each one includes is shown in the billing section of Settings.

items.question: How do I pay?
answer: Choose a plan in the billing section; the system creates an order and takes you to the payment gateway to scan a code or transfer as instructed.
Once the transaction succeeds you are returned to NaHo and the plan is activated for the account you are signed in with.

items.question: I paid but my account has not been upgraded
answer: Confirmation from the payment gateway can take a few minutes. Reload the page and check the order status in “Transaction history”.
If the order shows as successful but the plan is still not active after about 15 minutes, send a report with the order code and a screenshot of the receipt.

items.question: Where can I find my invoices and past transactions?
answer: Open the account menu in the top right corner and choose “Transaction history”. It lists the order code, amount, time and status of every transaction.
Keep the order code handy whenever you contact support about a payment issue.

items.question: Can I cancel a plan or request a refund?
answer: You can cancel an unpaid order directly in “Transaction history”. For an active plan, your benefits remain until the period you paid for ends.
Refund requests are reviewed according to the Terms of Service. Send a report with the order code and your reason so the NaHo team can process it.

items.question: How do I change my password?
answer: Go to Settings, open the security section and enter your current password together with the new one.
After changing your password, sign out of other devices if you suspect someone else has used your account.

items.question: What if I forgot my password?
answer: On the sign-in screen choose “Forgot password”, enter your registered email and follow the instructions sent to your inbox.
The reset link is only valid for a short time. If it expires, start the process again to receive a new one.

items.question: I did not receive the email verification code
answer: Check your spam and promotions folders, and make sure the email address you entered has no typo.
If nothing arrives after a few minutes, use the resend button on the verification screen. The old code stops working as soon as a new one is sent.

items.question: How do I sign out of all devices?
answer: Go to Settings, open the security section and use the option to sign out of every session. All signed-in devices are returned to the login screen.
Use this right after changing your password if you have ever signed in on a public computer.

items.question: Why do I see “your account is signed in elsewhere”?
answer: A NaHo account keeps only one active learning session at a time. When another device signs in, the older session ends and this warning appears.
If that sign-in was not you, change your password immediately and sign out of all devices.

items.question: How are my voice recordings used?
answer: Recordings are used to score your pronunciation and to build the report for your own practice session.
Details on how NaHo collects, stores and protects your data are set out in the Privacy Policy.

troubleshooting.title: Microphone & audio troubleshooting
troubleshooting.description: NaHo needs your microphone to score pronunciation. Here are the most common problems and how to fix them.
troubleshooting.browserDescription: Pick the browser you are using to see the exact steps.

items.title: NaHo does not pick up my voice
items.symptom: You speak but the waveform stays flat, or the result comes back empty.
steps: Check the microphone icon in the browser address bar and make sure permission is set to allow.
If your machine has several input devices, select the microphone you are actually using in your system sound settings.
Close apps that hold the microphone such as Zoom, Google Meet or Discord, then reload the page.
Try a new tab or a different browser to rule out a problem with the current session.

items.title: I cannot hear the AI voice
items.symptom: The session runs normally but no sound comes out.
steps: Check the system volume and make sure the NaHo tab is not muted (right-click the tab to check).
If you use Bluetooth headphones, disconnect and reconnect them, or try wired headphones.
Select the correct output device in your system sound settings.
Reload the page and start the session again.

items.title: My pronunciation score is unusually low
items.symptom: You pronounce correctly but the score comes back far below your usual level.
steps: Record in a quiet place; background noise and echo directly reduce recognition accuracy.
Keep the microphone about a hand-span from your mouth — neither too close nor too far.
Speak the whole sentence at an even pace; hesitating mid-sentence is often recognised as missing words.
If you use the built-in laptop microphone, try a headset microphone and compare the results.

items.title: The recording stops halfway
items.symptom: The session ends abruptly, or only the beginning of your sentence is captured.
steps: Check your network connection; an unstable link can interrupt the session.
Keep the NaHo tab visible and do not switch to another tab while recording.
Disable extensions that block device access or that throttle background tabs to save battery.
If it keeps happening, send a report with the time it occurred so the NaHo team can check the logs.

browsers.name: Chrome / Edge
steps: Click the lock or device icon at the start of the address bar.
Find the Microphone entry and switch it to Allow.
Reload the page so the browser applies the new permission.

browsers.name: Safari
steps: Open Safari in the menu bar, choose Settings and go to the Websites tab.
Select Microphone in the left column and set NaHo to Allow.
Close the settings window and reload NaHo.

browsers.name: Firefox
steps: Click the lock icon at the start of the address bar.
Remove the microphone block if you previously chose Block.
Reload the page and choose Allow when the browser asks again.
